Your social standing in your youth does not matter. Learning to navigate social dynamics does, but how popular you actually are will have little to no effect on the rest of your life except for how you let it shape your mind.  In a few years you will likely know almost nobody from your previous educational environment. The friendships that do last will probably not be the ones you expect to. Friendships formed from activities, social status, proximity, convenience, fun....  those die quickly. It's only the ones that are formed on what I would call an intellectual level that have a chance of surviving, and that is rare too. People change, if the two of you change too much even that intellectual connection breaks.  Again, the experience of making and having friends is hugely important, but the friendships themselves are far from permanent.  Because of this, cultivate your friendships. Know which ones to let die or just take a back burner and focus on the ones with a deeper connection. Meet as many people as you can. Get to know as many people as you can. Be open (within reason) to new experiences but be wary of anything addictive. Your life is teeming with potential right now, take advantage of it. In the future when you look back you will not regret the things you've done, but the things you didn't do.  This is all based off my own experience, I hope some of it helps you.
